lessons.title: Expanded Form and Standard Form
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

The expanded form of a number shows the value of each digit added together. Read the digits from the left by place value: ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, and write each digit multiplied by its place. The standard form is the opposite: add the expanded parts together to write the number in its usual short form.

Worked example: Numbers in expanded form (Exercise 1, Q1)

Step 1: (a) 75,432 = 7 ten-thousands + 5 thousands + 4 hundreds + 3 tens + 2 ones = 70,000 + 5,000 + 400 + 30 + 2
Step 2: (b) 37,911 = 3 ten-thousands + 7 thousands + 9 hundreds + 1 ten + 1 one = 30,000 + 7,000 + 900 + 10 + 1
Step 3: (c) 10,956 = 1 ten-thousand + 0 thousands + 9 hundreds + 5 tens + 6 ones = 10,000 + 0 + 900 + 50 + 6
Step 4: (d) 46,743 = 4 ten-thousands + 6 thousands + 7 hundreds + 4 tens + 3 ones = 40,000 + 6,000 + 700 + 40 + 3
Step 5: (e) 86,594 = 8 ten-thousands + 6 thousands + 5 hundreds + 9 tens + 4 ones = 80,000 + 6,000 + 500 + 90 + 4
Step 6: (f) 19,223 = 1 ten-thousand + 9 thousands + 2 hundreds + 2 tens + 3 ones = 10,000 + 9,000 + 200 + 20 + 3
Step 7: (g) 22,167 = 2 ten-thousands + 2 thousands + 1 hundred + 6 tens + 7 ones = 20,000 + 2,000 + 100 + 60 + 7
Step 8: (h) 57,890 = 5 ten-thousands + 7 thousands + 8 hundreds + 9 tens + 0 ones = 50,000 + 7,000 + 800 + 90 + 0
Step 9: (i) 36,789 = 3 ten-thousands + 6 thousands + 7 hundreds + 8 tens + 9 ones = 30,000 + 6,000 + 700 + 80 + 9
Step 10: (j) 78,324 = 7 ten-thousands + 8 thousands + 3 hundreds + 2 tens + 4 ones = 70,000 + 8,000 + 300 + 20 + 4
Step 11: (k) 41,452 = 4 ten-thousands + 1 thousand + 4 hundreds + 5 tens + 2 ones = 40,000 + 1,000 + 400 + 50 + 2
Step 12: (l) 56,432 = 5 ten-thousands + 6 thousands + 4 hundreds + 3 tens + 2 ones = 50,000 + 6,000 + 400 + 30 + 2
Answer: 75,432 = 70,000 + 5,000 + 400 + 30 + 2; 37,911 = 30,000 + 7,000 + 900 + 10 + 1; 10,956 = 10,000 + 0 + 900 + 50 + 6; 46,743 = 40,000 + 6,000 + 700 + 40 + 3; 86,594 = 80,000 + 6,000 + 500 + 90 + 4; 19,223 = 10,000 + 9,000 + 200 + 20 + 3; 22,167 = 20,000 + 2,000 + 100 + 60 + 7; 57,890 = 50,000 + 7,000 + 800 + 90 + 0; 36,789 = 30,000 + 6,000 + 700 + 80 + 9; 78,324 = 70,000 + 8,000 + 300 + 20 + 4; 41,452 = 40,000 + 1,000 + 400 + 50 + 2; 56,432 = 50,000 + 6,000 + 400 + 30 + 2

Worked example: Expanded form to standard form (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: (a) 20,000 + 1,000 + 100 + 70 + 1 = 21,171
Step 2: (b) 30,000 + 9,000 + 200 + 30 + 5 = 39,235
Step 3: (c) 60,000 + 5,000 + 300 + 40 + 3 = 65,343
Step 4: (d) 50,000 + 6,000 + 700 + 90 + 0 = 56,790
Answer: 21,171; 39,235; 65,343; 56,790

mcqs.why: The digits of 10,956 are 1 ten-thousand, 0 thousands, 9 hundreds, 5 tens and 6 ones. The thousands digit is 0 and 0 x 1,000 = 0, so 10,956 = 10,000 + 0 + 900 + 50 + 6.

mcqs.why: In 86,594 the digit 6 stands at the thousands place, so its value is 6 x 1,000 = 6,000.

What does the expanded form of a number show?

lessons.title: Place and Place Value
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

The place of a digit tells where it stands in the number: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands or ten-thousands, counting from the right. The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by its place, for example a digit at the thousands place has place value digit x 1,000.

Worked example: Place and place value of the coloured digits (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: (a) 76,102 (coloured digit 0): The coloured digit is 0. It is at the tens place. Its place value = 0 x 10 = 0
Step 2: (b) 24,360 (coloured digit 2): The coloured digit is 2. It is at the ten-thousands place. Its place value = 2 x 10,000 = 20,000
Step 3: (c) 94,615 (coloured digit 4): The coloured digit is 4. It is at the thousands place. Its place value = 4 x 1,000 = 4,000
Step 4: (d) 65,496 (coloured digit 6): The coloured digit is 6. It is at the ones place. Its place value = 6 x 1 = 6
Step 5: (e) 73,456 (coloured digit 7): The coloured digit is 7. It is at the ten-thousands place. Its place value = 7 x 10,000 = 70,000
Step 6: (f) 18,654 (coloured digit 8): The coloured digit is 8. It is at the thousands place. Its place value = 8 x 1,000 = 8,000
Step 7: (g) 34,566 (coloured digit 5): The coloured digit is 5. It is at the hundreds place. Its place value = 5 x 100 = 500
Step 8: (h) 86,042 (coloured digit 6): The coloured digit is 6. It is at the thousands place. Its place value = 6 x 1,000 = 6,000
Step 9: (i) 56,324 (coloured digit 4): The coloured digit is 4. It is at the ones place. Its place value = 4 x 1 = 4
Answer: (a) 0 at tens place, place value 0; (b) 2 at ten-thousands place, place value 20,000; (c) 4 at thousands place, place value 4,000; (d) 6 at ones place, place value 6; (e) 7 at ten-thousands place, place value 70,000; (f) 8 at thousands place, place value 8,000; (g) 5 at hundreds place, place value 500; (h) 6 at thousands place, place value 6,000; (i) 4 at ones place, place value 4

mcqs.q: In 76,102, the digit 0 is at which place?
mcqs.why: Counting from the right in 76,102: 2 is ones, 0 is tens, 1 is hundreds, 6 is thousands and 7 is ten-thousands, so 0 is at the tens place.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the digit 2 in 24,360?
mcqs.why: The digit 2 is at the ten-thousands place, so its place value is 2 x 10,000 = 20,000.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the digit 4 in 94,615?
mcqs.why: The digit 4 is at the thousands place, so its place value is 4 x 1,000 = 4,000.

mcqs.q: In 65,496, the digit 6 at the ones place has place value:
mcqs.why: A digit at the ones place is multiplied by 1, so the place value is 6 x 1 = 6.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the digit 7 in 73,456?
mcqs.why: The digit 7 is the first digit from the left in a 5-digit number, so it is at the ten-thousands place: 7 x 10,000 = 70,000.

mcqs.q: In 34,566, the digit 5 is at the hundreds place. Its place value is:
mcqs.why: Place value is the digit multiplied by its place: 5 x 100 = 500.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the digit 8 in 18,654?
mcqs.why: In 18,654 the digit 8 stands at the thousands place, so its place value is 8 x 1,000 = 8,000.

mcqs.q: The place value of a digit is found by:
options: Adding the digit to its place
Dividing the digit by its place
Multiplying the digit by its place
Writing the digit as it is
mcqs.why: Place value is the digit multiplied by its place; for example, a digit at the thousands place has place value digit x 1,000.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the digit 6 in 86,042?
mcqs.why: In 86,042 the digit 6 is at the thousands place, so its place value is 6 x 1,000 = 6,000.

mcqs.q: In 56,324, which digit is at the ones place, and what is its place value?
mcqs.why: The last digit on the right is the ones digit. In 56,324 it is 4, and its place value is 4 x 1 = 4.

lessons.title: Numbers in Words and Numerals
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

To write a 5-digit number in words, split it into the thousands part and the last three digits: write the thousands part in words followed by thousand, then write the remaining hundreds, tens and ones in words. To write words in numerals, do the reverse: write the thousands part as a number, then fill the hundreds, tens and ones places, using 0 for any place that is not named.

Worked example: Numbers in words (Exercise 1, Q4)

Step 1: (a) 74,325 = 74 thousand + 325 = seventy-four thousand three hundred twenty-five
Step 2: (b) 43,711 = 43 thousand + 711 = forty-three thousand seven hundred eleven
Step 3: (c) 19,560 = 19 thousand + 560 = nineteen thousand five hundred sixty
Step 4: (d) 75,434 = 75 thousand + 434 = seventy-five thousand four hundred thirty-four
Step 5: (e) 67,459 = 67 thousand + 459 = sixty-seven thousand four hundred fifty-nine
Step 6: (f) 25,302 = 25 thousand + 302 = twenty-five thousand three hundred two
Step 7: (g) 36,721 = 36 thousand + 721 = thirty-six thousand seven hundred twenty-one
Step 8: (h) 78,065 = 78 thousand + 65 = seventy-eight thousand sixty-five
Step 9: (i) 62,897 = 62 thousand + 897 = sixty-two thousand eight hundred ninety-seven
Step 10: (j) 37,264 = 37 thousand + 264 = thirty-seven thousand two hundred sixty-four
Step 11: (k) 45,129 = 45 thousand + 129 = forty-five thousand one hundred twenty-nine
Step 12: (l) 43,275 = 43 thousand + 275 = forty-three thousand two hundred seventy-five
Answer: seventy-four thousand three hundred twenty-five; forty-three thousand seven hundred eleven; nineteen thousand five hundred sixty; seventy-five thousand four hundred thirty-four; sixty-seven thousand four hundred fifty-nine; twenty-five thousand three hundred two; thirty-six thousand seven hundred twenty-one; seventy-eight thousand sixty-five; sixty-two thousand eight hundred ninety-seven; thirty-seven thousand two hundred sixty-four; forty-five thousand one hundred twenty-nine; forty-three thousand two hundred seventy-five

Worked example: Words in numerals (Exercise 1, Q5)

Step 1: (a) Twenty-five thousand six hundred = 25 thousand + 600 = 25,600
Step 2: (b) Seventy-eight thousand four hundred two = 78 thousand + 402 = 78,402
Step 3: (c) Forty-one thousand sixty-one = 41 thousand + 61 = 41,061
Step 4: (d) Ninety-eight thousand three hundred one = 98 thousand + 301 = 98,301
Step 5: (e) Seventy-two thousand five hundred forty-six = 72 thousand + 546 = 72,546
Step 6: (f) Twelve thousand five hundred fifty-five = 12 thousand + 555 = 12,555
Step 7: (g) Ninety-eight thousand five = 98 thousand + 5 = 98,005
Step 8: (h) Forty-eight thousand four hundred forty-four = 48 thousand + 444 = 48,444
Step 9: (i) Eighty-eight thousand three hundred twenty = 88 thousand + 320 = 88,320
Answer: 25,600; 78,402; 41,061; 98,301; 72,546; 12,555; 98,005; 48,444; 88,320

mcqs.why: Twenty-five thousand gives 25,000 and six hundred gives 600; 25,000 + 600 = 25,600. The tens and ones places stay 0.

mcqs.why: 78,065 = 78 thousand + 65. There is no hundreds part, so it reads seventy-eight thousand sixty-five.

mcqs.why: Forty-one thousand gives 41,000 and sixty-one gives 61; 41,000 + 61 = 41,061. The hundreds place is not named, so it is filled with 0.

lessons.title: Comparing Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

To compare two numbers, compare from the left, starting at the greatest place value. A number with more digits is greater. If the digits at a place are equal, move to the next place on the right until a difference is found. Use < for smaller, > for greater and = for equal.

Worked example: Comparing numbers with symbols (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: (a) 84,325 ___ 93,417: Compare from the left: at the ten-thousands place 8 < 9, so 84,325 is smaller. 84,325 < 93,417
Step 2: (b) 4,853 ___ 19,314: A 4-digit number is always smaller than a 5-digit number. 4,853 < 19,314
Step 3: (c) 56,708 ___ 32,156: At the ten-thousands place 5 > 3, so 56,708 is greater. 56,708 > 32,156
Step 4: (d) 23,612 ___ 23,612: Both numbers are exactly the same. 23,612 = 23,612
Step 5: (e) 65,356 ___ 65,358: Ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens are equal; at the ones place 6 < 8. 65,356 < 65,358
Step 6: (f) 74,932 ___ 74,542: Ten-thousands and thousands are equal; at the hundreds place 9 > 5. 74,932 > 74,542
Step 7: (g) 68,709 ___ 68,709: Both numbers are exactly the same. 68,709 = 68,709
Step 8: (h) 32,567 ___ 23,578: At the ten-thousands place 3 > 2, so 32,567 is greater. 32,567 > 23,578
Answer: 84,325 < 93,417; 4,853 < 19,314; 56,708 > 32,156; 23,612 = 23,612; 65,356 < 65,358; 74,932 > 74,542; 68,709 = 68,709; 32,567 > 23,578

mcqs.q: Which comparison is correct?
mcqs.why: Compare from the left: at the ten-thousands place 8 is less than 9, so 84,325 is smaller than 93,417.

mcqs.q: 4,853 ___ 19,314. Which symbol fills the blank?
mcqs.why: A 4-digit number is always smaller than a 5-digit number, so 4,853 < 19,314.

mcqs.q: Which comparison is correct?
mcqs.why: In 65,356 and 65,358 all places are equal until the ones place, where 6 is less than 8, so 65,356 < 65,358.

mcqs.q: 23,612 ___ 23,612. Which symbol fills the blank?
mcqs.why: Both numbers are exactly the same, digit for digit, so the equal sign is used: 23,612 = 23,612.

mcqs.q: To compare two numbers, we start comparing from:
options: The greatest place value on the left
mcqs.why: The rule is to compare from the left, starting at the greatest place value, and move to the next place on the right only while the digits stay equal.

mcqs.q: Which comparison is correct?
mcqs.why: In 74,932 and 74,542 the ten-thousands and thousands digits are equal; at the hundreds place 9 is greater than 5, so 74,932 > 74,542.

mcqs.q: A number with more digits is:
mcqs.why: More digits means a greater place value is present; for example, the 5-digit number 19,314 is greater than the 4-digit number 4,853.

mcqs.q: 32,567 ___ 23,578. Which symbol fills the blank?
mcqs.why: At the ten-thousands place 3 is greater than 2, so 32,567 > 23,578.

mcqs.q: In 65,356 and 65,358, the first place where the digits differ is:
mcqs.why: Ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens digits are all equal; the ones digits 6 and 8 differ, so the ones place decides the comparison.

mcqs.q: Which symbol means 'is smaller than'?
mcqs.why: The symbol < is used for smaller, > is used for greater, and = is used for equal numbers.

mcqs.q: Ascending order means writing numbers:
mcqs.why: Ascending order arranges numbers from smallest to greatest; descending order is the reverse, from greatest to smallest.

mcqs.q: Which list is in ascending order?
mcqs.why: 31,273 is the smallest. Between 40,131 and 40,735 the hundreds digits 1 and 7 decide, and 40,131 < 40,735, so the order is 31,273; 40,131; 40,735.

mcqs.q: Which list is in descending order?
mcqs.why: Descending order goes from greatest to smallest: 97,035 is greatest, then 83,401, then 12,337.

mcqs.q: Which list is in ascending order?
mcqs.why: Compare the ten-thousands digits: 2 is smallest, then 3, then 4, giving the ascending order 28,211; 30,817; 43,181.

mcqs.q: Which list is in descending order?
mcqs.why: 18,221 and 18,017 tie until the hundreds place, where 2 is greater than 0, so 18,221 comes first; 13,411 is the smallest.

mcqs.q: Which number is the smallest in 89,675; 84,675; 89,546?
mcqs.why: 84,675 has 4 at the thousands place while the other two numbers have 9 there, so 84,675 is the smallest of the three.

mcqs.q: In ascending order, 89,546 comes just before 89,675 because:
options: At the tens place 4 is less than 7
mcqs.why: The two numbers agree until the tens place, where 4 is less than 7, so 89,546 < 89,675 and it comes first in ascending order.

mcqs.q: Which list is in descending order?
mcqs.why: 24,391 and 24,313 agree until the tens place, where 9 is greater than 1, so 24,391 is greater; 12,683 is the smallest.

mcqs.q: Which list is in ascending order?
mcqs.why: The ten-thousands digits are 2, 5 and 6, so from smallest to greatest the order is 24,085; 59,312; 60,337.

mcqs.q: To arrange numbers in order, we compare them:
options: From the left, by place value
mcqs.why: Ordering uses the same comparison as comparing numbers: start at the greatest place on the left and move right while the digits are equal.

lessons.title: Adding 5-Digit Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Method: add column by column from the ones place, carrying to the next place whenever a column total is 10 or more. Write the numbers one below the other so that ones are under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds, thousands under thousands and ten-thousands under ten-thousands. Always start from the ones place on the right.

Worked example: 13,927 + 2,415 (Exercise 1, Q1a)

Step 1: Ones place: 7 + 5 = 12. Write 2 and carry 1.
Step 2: Tens place: 2 + 1 + 1 (carry) = 4. Write 4.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 9 + 4 = 13. Write 3 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 3 + 2 + 1 (carry) = 6. Write 6.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 1 + 0 = 1. Write 1.
Answer: 16,342

Worked example: 35,321 + 4,649 (Exercise 1, Q1b)

Step 1: Ones place: 1 + 9 = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 2: Tens place: 2 + 4 + 1 (carry) = 7. Write 7.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 3 + 6 = 9. Write 9.
Step 4: Thousands place: 5 + 4 = 9. Write 9.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 3 + 0 = 3. Write 3.
Answer: 39,970

Worked example: 75,679 + 16,828 (Exercise 1, Q1c)

Step 1: Ones place: 9 + 8 = 17. Write 7 and carry 1.
Step 2: Tens place: 7 + 2 + 1 (carry) = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 6 + 8 + 1 (carry) = 15. Write 5 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 5 + 6 + 1 (carry) = 12. Write 2 and carry 1.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 7 + 1 + 1 (carry) = 9. Write 9.
Answer: 92,507

Ones: 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 3 + 6 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Hundreds: 1 + 3 + 1 = 5. Thousands: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Ten-thousands: 5 + 4 + 1 = 10, so write 0 and carry 1 to make 103,501.

lessons.title: Addition Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Read the question carefully. Write what is given and what you have to find. When two amounts are joined together to make a total, we add them. Add column by column from the ones place, carrying to the next place whenever a column total is 10 or more. At the end, write the answer as a full sentence with its unit (Rs, passengers, books or km).

Worked example: Nida's laptop and repairing cost (Exercise 1, Q3)

Given: Nida bought a laptop for Rs 59,453 and spent Rs 12,652 on repairing. To find: the total amount she spent. Operation: addition — add the two amounts: 59,453 + 12,652.

Step 1: Ones place: 3 + 2 = 5. Write 5.
Step 2: Tens place: 5 + 5 = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 4 + 6 + 1 (carry) = 11. Write 1 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 9 + 2 + 1 (carry) = 12. Write 2 and carry 1.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 5 + 1 + 1 (carry) = 7. Write 7.
Answer: Nida spent Rs 72,105 in total.

Worked example: Passengers in two months (Exercise 1, Q4)

Given: In January, 83,215 people travelled from an airport and in February, 21,084 people travelled. To find: how many passengers travelled in two months. Operation: addition — add: 83,215 + 21,084.

Step 1: Ones place: 5 + 4 = 9. Write 9.
Step 2: Tens place: 1 + 8 = 9. Write 9.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 2 + 0 = 2. Write 2.
Step 4: Thousands place: 3 + 1 = 4. Write 4.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 8 + 2 = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 6: Ten-thousands carry: write 1.
Answer: 104,299 passengers travelled in two months.

Worked example: Books in the library (Exercise 1, Q5a)

Given: In a library, there are 42,725 books. The administration decided to add 22,500 new books. To find: the total number of books in the library. Operation: addition — add: 42,725 + 22,500.

Step 1: Ones place: 5 + 0 = 5. Write 5.
Step 2: Tens place: 2 + 0 = 2. Write 2.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 7 + 5 = 12. Write 2 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 2 + 2 + 1 (carry) = 5. Write 5.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 4 + 2 = 6. Write 6.
Answer: There are 65,225 books in the library in total.

Worked example: More books added to the library (Exercise 1, Q5b)

Given: The library now has 65,225 books (from Q5a) and 23,890 more books are added. To find: the new total number of books. Operation: addition — add: 65,225 + 23,890.

Step 1: Ones place: 5 + 0 = 5. Write 5.
Step 2: Tens place: 2 + 9 = 11. Write 1 and carry 1.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 2 + 8 + 1 (carry) = 11. Write 1 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 5 + 3 + 1 (carry) = 9. Write 9.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 6 + 2 = 8. Write 8.
Answer: There are 89,115 books in the library in total.

Worked example: Distance covered by a bus in two months (Exercise 1, Q6a)

Given: A bus covered 23,672 km distance in the first month and 31,716 km in the second month. To find: the total distance covered in two months. Operation: addition — add: 23,672 + 31,716.

Step 1: Ones place: 2 + 6 = 8. Write 8.
Step 2: Tens place: 7 + 1 = 8. Write 8.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 6 + 7 = 13. Write 3 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 3 + 1 + 1 (carry) = 5. Write 5.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 2 + 3 = 5. Write 5.
Answer: The bus covered 55,388 km in two months in total.

Worked example: In which month did the bus cover more distance? (Exercise 1, Q6b)

Given: First month = 23,672 km. Second month = 31,716 km. To find: which month has the bigger distance. Operation: compare the two numbers — 31,716 is more than 23,672.

Step 1: Compare the ten-thousands place: both numbers start with 2 and 3 in the ten-thousands and thousands places — 31,716 has 3 ten-thousands, while 23,672 has 2 ten-thousands, so 31,716 is the bigger number.
Answer: The bus covered more distance in the second month (31,716 km).

lessons.title: Subtraction Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Read the question carefully. Write what is given and what you have to find. When an amount is spent, taken away, or we ask how much is left or how much more, we subtract. Subtract column by column from the ones place, borrowing from the next place whenever the upper digit is smaller. At the end, write the answer as a full sentence with its unit.

Worked example: Money left with Saad after buying a bicycle (Exercise 2, Q3a)

Given: Saad had Rs 52,490. He bought a bicycle for Rs 15,873. To find: how much money was left with him. Operation: subtraction — subtract: 52,490 - 15,873.

Step 1: Ones place: 0 is less than 3, so borrow 1 from the next place: 10 - 3 = 7. Write 7.
Step 2: Tens place: 9 - 1 (borrow) = 8, then 8 - 7 = 1. Write 1.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 4 is less than 8, so borrow 1 from the next place: 14 - 8 = 6. Write 6.
Step 4: Thousands place: 2 - 1 (borrow) = 1, which is less than 5, so borrow 1 from the next place: 11 - 5 = 6. Write 6.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 5 - 1 (borrow) = 4, then 4 - 1 = 3. Write 3.
Answer: Rs 36,617 was left with Saad.

Worked example: Money left if the bicycle costs Rs 18,759 (Exercise 2, Q3b)

Given: Saad had Rs 52,490. The price of the bicycle is Rs 18,759. To find: how much money will be left. Operation: subtraction — subtract: 52,490 - 18,759.

Step 1: Ones place: 0 is less than 9, so borrow 1 from the next place: 10 - 9 = 1. Write 1.
Step 2: Tens place: 9 - 1 (borrow) = 8, then 8 - 5 = 3. Write 3.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 4 is less than 7, so borrow 1 from the next place: 14 - 7 = 7. Write 7.
Step 4: Thousands place: 2 - 1 (borrow) = 1, which is less than 8, so borrow 1 from the next place: 11 - 8 = 3. Write 3.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 5 - 1 (borrow) = 4, then 4 - 1 = 3. Write 3.
Answer: Rs 33,731 will be left with Saad.

Worked example: Rice bags in a godown (Exercise 2, Q4)

Given: In a godown, there are 66,375 bags of wheat and rice. The number of wheat bags is 44,468. To find: the number of rice bags. Operation: subtraction — subtract the wheat bags from the total bags: 66,375 - 44,468.

Step 1: Ones place: 5 is less than 8, so borrow 1 from the next place: 15 - 8 = 7. Write 7.
Step 2: Tens place: 7 - 1 (borrow) = 6, then 6 - 6 = 0. Write 0.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 3 is less than 4, so borrow 1 from the next place: 13 - 4 = 9. Write 9.
Step 4: Thousands place: 6 - 1 (borrow) = 5, then 5 - 4 = 1. Write 1.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 6 - 4 = 2. Write 2.
Answer: There are 21,907 rice bags in the godown.

Worked example: How much more did Class 3 collect than Class 4? (Exercise 2, Q5)

Given: The students of Class 3 collected Rs 35,278 for a welfare institution, while the students of Class 4 collected Rs 32,184. To find: how much more amount was collected by Class 3 than Class 4. Operation: subtraction — subtract: 35,278 - 32,184.

Step 1: Ones place: 8 - 4 = 4. Write 4.
Step 2: Tens place: 7 is less than 8, so borrow 1 from the next place: 17 - 8 = 9. Write 9.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 2 - 1 (borrow) = 1, then 1 - 1 = 0. Write 0.
Step 4: Thousands place: 5 - 2 = 3. Write 3.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 3 - 3 = 0. Write 0.
Answer: Class 3 collected Rs 3,094 more than Class 4.

Worked example: How many more votes did the second candidate get? (Exercise 2, Q6)

Given: One candidate got 62,436 votes from a constituency, while the other candidate got 86,733 votes. To find: how many more votes the second candidate got than the first candidate. Operation: subtraction — subtract the smaller number from the bigger number: 86,733 - 62,436.

Step 1: Ones place: 3 is less than 6, so borrow 1 from the next place: 13 - 6 = 7. Write 7.
Step 2: Tens place: 3 - 1 (borrow) = 2, which is less than 3, so borrow 1 from the next place: 12 - 3 = 9. Write 9.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 7 - 1 (borrow) = 6, then 6 - 4 = 2. Write 2.
Step 4: Thousands place: 6 - 2 = 4. Write 4.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 8 - 6 = 2. Write 2.
Answer: The second candidate got 24,297 more votes than the first candidate.

mcqs.why: Spending, taking away, how much is left and how much more are all found by subtraction, done column by column from the ones place with borrowing when needed.

lessons.title: Multiplying by 1-Digit, 2-Digit and 3-Digit Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Method: multiply by place value — multiply the multiplicand by each digit of the multiplier, then add the partial products. First multiply by the ones digit, then by the tens digit (which means multiplying by tens, so the answer ends with one zero), then by the hundreds digit (which means multiplying by hundreds, so the answer ends with two zeros). In the end, add all the partial products to get the final product.

Worked example: 631 x 4 (Exercise 1, Q1a)

Step 1: Multiply 631 by 4 (4 ones): 631 x 4 = 2,524.
Answer: 2,524

Worked example: 431 x 35 (Exercise 1, Q1b)

Step 1: Multiply 431 by 5 (5 ones): 431 x 5 = 2,155.
Step 2: Multiply 431 by 30 (3 tens): 431 x 30 = 12,930.
Step 3: Add the partial products: 2,155 + 12,930 = 15,085.
Answer: 15,085

Worked example: 8,434 x 31 (Exercise 1, Q1c)

Step 3: Add the partial products: 8,434 + 253,020 = 261,454.

Step 2: Multiply 8,046 by 70 (7 tens): 8,046 x 70 = 563,220.
Step 3: Multiply 8,046 by 600 (6 hundreds): 8,046 x 600 = 4,827,600.
Step 4: Add the partial products: 64,368 + 563,220 + 4,827,600 = 5,455,188.
Answer: 5,455,188

Worked example: 7,601 x 546 (Exercise 1, Q1e)

Step 1: Multiply 7,601 by 6 (6 ones): 7,601 x 6 = 45,606.

Worked example: 41,175 x 80 (Exercise 1, Q1f)

Answer: 3,294,000

Worked example: 79,762 x 15 (Exercise 1, Q1g)

Step 2: Multiply 79,762 by 10 (1 tens): 79,762 x 10 = 797,620.

Step 1: Multiply 63,506 by 3 (3 ones): 63,506 x 3 = 190,518.
Step 2: Multiply 63,506 by 0 (0 tens): 63,506 x 0 = 0, so there is no tens partial product to add.
Step 3: Multiply 63,506 by 300 (3 hundreds): 63,506 x 300 = 19,051,800.

Step 1: Multiply 11,098 by 7 (7 ones): 11,098 x 7 = 77,686.
Step 2: Multiply 11,098 by 30 (3 tens): 11,098 x 30 = 332,940.
Step 3: Multiply 11,098 by 200 (2 hundreds): 11,098 x 200 = 2,219,600.
Step 4: Add the partial products: 77,686 + 332,940 + 2,219,600 = 2,630,226.
Answer: 2,630,226

Worked example: Try It! challenge — find the missing circles (book page 29)

In this puzzle, the number in each box is the product of the numbers in the two circles next to it. Two boxes are given: 2,808 and 2,340, and one circle is given as 12. We have to find the two blank circles.

Step 1: The box 2,808 sits between the top circle and the circle 12, so: top circle x 12 = 2,808.
Step 2: Find the top circle: 2,808 divided by 12 = 234. Check: 234 x 12 = 2,808. So the top circle is 234.
Step 3: The box 2,340 sits between the top circle 234 and the other blank circle, so: 234 x blank circle = 2,340.
Step 4: Find the blank circle: 2,340 divided by 234 = 10. Check: 234 x 10 = 2,340. So the other blank circle is 10.
Answer: The top circle is 234 and the other blank circle is 10.

lessons.title: Multiplication Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Read the question carefully. Write what is given and what you have to find. When the same amount is repeated many times — for example, the same earning for many days — we multiply. Multiply by place value: multiply by each digit of the multiplier, then add the partial products. At the end, write the answer as a full sentence with its unit.

Worked example: Cloth sold in 21 weeks (Exercise 1, Q2)

Given: A shopkeeper sold 34,523 m cloth in a week. To find: how much cloth he will sell in 21 weeks. Operation: multiplication — multiply: 34,523 x 21.

Step 1: Multiply 34,523 by 1 (1 ones): 34,523 x 1 = 34,523.
Step 2: Multiply 34,523 by 20 (2 tens): 34,523 x 20 = 690,460.
Step 3: Add the partial products: 34,523 + 690,460 = 724,983.
Answer: The shopkeeper will sell 724,983 m cloth in 21 weeks.

Worked example: Majid's earning in 365 days (Exercise 1, Q3a)

Given: Majid earns Rs 11,045 in a day. To find: how much money he will earn in 365 days. Operation: multiplication — multiply: 11,045 x 365.

Step 1: Multiply 11,045 by 5 (5 ones): 11,045 x 5 = 55,225.
Step 2: Multiply 11,045 by 60 (6 tens): 11,045 x 60 = 662,700.
Step 3: Multiply 11,045 by 300 (3 hundreds): 11,045 x 300 = 3,313,500.
Step 4: Add the partial products: 55,225 + 662,700 + 3,313,500 = 4,031,425.
Answer: Majid will earn Rs 4,031,425 in 365 days.

Worked example: Majid's earning in 2 years (Exercise 1, Q3b)

Given: Majid earns Rs 11,045 in a day. 2 years = 730 days. To find: how much money he will earn in 2 years. Operation: multiplication — multiply: 11,045 x 730.

Step 1: Multiply 11,045 by 0 (0 ones): 11,045 x 0 = 0, so there is no ones partial product to add.
Step 2: Multiply 11,045 by 30 (3 tens): 11,045 x 30 = 331,350.
Step 3: Multiply 11,045 by 700 (7 hundreds): 11,045 x 700 = 7,731,500.
Step 4: Add the partial products: 331,350 + 7,731,500 = 8,062,850.
Answer: Majid will earn Rs 8,062,850 in 2 years.

Worked example: Notebooks printed in 210 days (Exercise 1, Q4)

Given: In a factory, 20,134 notebooks were printed in a day. To find: how many notebooks will be printed in 210 days. Operation: multiplication — multiply: 20,134 x 210.

Step 1: Multiply 20,134 by 0 (0 ones): 20,134 x 0 = 0, so there is no ones partial product to add.
Step 2: Multiply 20,134 by 10 (1 tens): 20,134 x 10 = 201,340.
Step 3: Multiply 20,134 by 200 (2 hundreds): 20,134 x 200 = 4,026,800.
Step 4: Add the partial products: 201,340 + 4,026,800 = 4,228,140.
Answer: 4,228,140 notebooks will be printed in 210 days.

Worked example: Money collected by 345 members for a tour (Exercise 1, Q5)

Given: Each member of a group gives Rs 34,156 for a tour of Naran and Kagan. There are 345 members of the group. To find: how much money the group will collect altogether. Operation: multiplication — multiply: 34,156 x 345.

Step 1: Multiply 34,156 by 5 (5 ones): 34,156 x 5 = 170,780.
Step 2: Multiply 34,156 by 40 (4 tens): 34,156 x 40 = 1,366,240.
Step 3: Multiply 34,156 by 300 (3 hundreds): 34,156 x 300 = 10,246,800.
Step 4: Add the partial products: 170,780 + 1,366,240 + 10,246,800 = 11,783,820.
Answer: The group will collect Rs 11,783,820 altogether.

lessons.title: Long Division
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Method: long division — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, repeat; the last remainder is written with the quotient. Start from the left side of the dividend. At each step, see how many times the divisor goes into the number, multiply, subtract to find the remainder, then bring down the next digit and repeat. Check your answer: quotient x divisor + remainder = dividend.

Worked example: 585 divided by 3 (Exercise 2, Q1a)

Step 1: 3 into 5 goes 1 time (1 x 3 = 3), remainder 2.
Step 2: Bring down 8: 3 into 28 goes 9 times (9 x 3 = 27), remainder 1.
Step 3: Bring down 5: 3 into 15 goes 5 times (5 x 3 = 15), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 195, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 1,816 divided by 4 (Exercise 2, Q1b)

Step 1: 4 into 18 goes 4 times (4 x 4 = 16), remainder 2.
Step 2: Bring down 1: 4 into 21 goes 5 times (5 x 4 = 20), remainder 1.
Step 3: Bring down 6: 4 into 16 goes 4 times (4 x 4 = 16), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 454, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 6,972 divided by 42 (Exercise 2, Q1c)

Step 1: 42 into 69 goes 1 time (1 x 42 = 42), remainder 27.
Step 2: Bring down 7: 42 into 277 goes 6 times (6 x 42 = 252), remainder 25.
Step 3: Bring down 2: 42 into 252 goes 6 times (6 x 42 = 252), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 166, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 7,546 divided by 22 (Exercise 2, Q1d)

Step 1: 22 into 75 goes 3 times (3 x 22 = 66), remainder 9.
Step 2: Bring down 4: 22 into 94 goes 4 times (4 x 22 = 88), remainder 6.
Step 3: Bring down 6: 22 into 66 goes 3 times (3 x 22 = 66), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 343, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 9,568 divided by 23 (Exercise 2, Q1e)

Step 1: 23 into 95 goes 4 times (4 x 23 = 92), remainder 3.
Step 2: Bring down 6: 23 into 36 goes 1 time (1 x 23 = 23), remainder 13.
Step 3: Bring down 8: 23 into 138 goes 6 times (6 x 23 = 138), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 416, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 9,641 divided by 31 (Exercise 2, Q1f)

Step 1: 31 into 96 goes 3 times (3 x 31 = 93), remainder 3.
Step 2: Bring down 4: 31 into 34 goes 1 time (1 x 31 = 31), remainder 3.
Step 3: Bring down 1: 31 into 31 goes 1 time (1 x 31 = 31), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 311, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 2,868 divided by 12 (Exercise 2, Q1g)

Step 1: 12 into 28 goes 2 times (2 x 12 = 24), remainder 4.
Step 2: Bring down 6: 12 into 46 goes 3 times (3 x 12 = 36), remainder 10.
Step 3: Bring down 8: 12 into 108 goes 9 times (9 x 12 = 108), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 239, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 7,392 divided by 32 (Exercise 2, Q1h)

Step 1: 32 into 73 goes 2 times (2 x 32 = 64), remainder 9.
Step 2: Bring down 9: 32 into 99 goes 3 times (3 x 32 = 96), remainder 3.
Step 3: Bring down 2: 32 into 32 goes 1 time (1 x 32 = 32), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 231, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 133 divided by 11 (Exercise 2, Q1i)

Step 1: 11 into 13 goes 1 time (1 x 11 = 11), remainder 2.
Step 2: Bring down 3: 11 into 23 goes 2 times (2 x 11 = 22), remainder 1.
Step 3: There is no more digit to bring down, so the last remainder is 1.
Answer: Quotient = 12, Remainder = 1

Worked example: 1,056 divided by 8 (Exercise 2, Q1j)

Step 1: 8 into 10 goes 1 time (1 x 8 = 8), remainder 2.
Step 2: Bring down 5: 8 into 25 goes 3 times (3 x 8 = 24), remainder 1.
Step 3: Bring down 6: 8 into 16 goes 2 times (2 x 8 = 16), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 132, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 1,848 divided by 88 (Exercise 2, Q1k)

Step 1: 88 into 184 goes 2 times (2 x 88 = 176), remainder 8.
Step 2: Bring down 8: 88 into 88 goes 1 time (1 x 88 = 88), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 21, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 4,662 divided by 42 (Exercise 2, Q1l)

Step 1: 42 into 46 goes 1 time (1 x 42 = 42), remainder 4.
Step 2: Bring down 6: 42 into 46 goes 1 time (1 x 42 = 42), remainder 4.
Step 3: Bring down 2: 42 into 42 goes 1 time (1 x 42 = 42), remainder 0.
Answer: Quotient = 111, Remainder = 0

Worked example: 6,125 divided by 10 (Exercise 2, Q1m)

Step 1: 10 into 61 goes 6 times (6 x 10 = 60), remainder 1.
Step 2: Bring down 2: 10 into 12 goes 1 time (1 x 10 = 10), remainder 2.
Step 3: Bring down 5: 10 into 25 goes 2 times (2 x 10 = 20), remainder 5.
Step 4: There is no more digit to bring down, so the last remainder is 5.
Answer: Quotient = 612, Remainder = 5

Worked example: 2,060 divided by 23 (Exercise 2, Q1n)

Step 1: 23 into 206 goes 8 times (8 x 23 = 184), remainder 22.
Step 2: Bring down 0: 23 into 220 goes 9 times (9 x 23 = 207), remainder 13.
Step 3: There is no more digit to bring down, so the last remainder is 13.
Answer: Quotient = 89, Remainder = 13

mcqs.q: What is 585 / 3?
mcqs.why: 3 into 5 goes 1 time, remainder 2. Bring down 8: 3 into 28 goes 9 times, remainder 1. Bring down 5: 3 into 15 goes 5 times, remainder 0. Quotient 195, remainder 0. Check: 195 x 3 = 585.

mcqs.q: What is 6,972 / 42?
mcqs.why: 42 into 69 goes 1 time, remainder 27. Bring down 7: 42 into 277 goes 6 times (6 x 42 = 252), remainder 25. Bring down 2: 42 into 252 goes 6 times, remainder 0. Quotient 166. Check: 166 x 42 = 6,972.

mcqs.q: What is 133 / 11?
mcqs.why: 11 into 13 goes 1 time, remainder 2. Bring down 3: 11 into 23 goes 2 times, remainder 1. No digit is left to bring down, so quotient 12, remainder 1. Check: 12 x 11 + 1 = 133.

mcqs.q: A division answer is checked by:
mcqs.why: The check is: quotient x divisor + remainder = dividend. If this gives back the dividend, the division is correct.

mcqs.q: What is 9,568 / 23?
mcqs.why: 23 into 95 goes 4 times (4 x 23 = 92), remainder 3. Bring down 6: 23 into 36 goes 1 time, remainder 13. Bring down 8: 23 into 138 goes 6 times, remainder 0. Quotient 416. Check: 416 x 23 = 9,568.

mcqs.q: What is 6,125 / 10?
mcqs.why: 10 into 61 goes 6 times, remainder 1. Bring down 2: 10 into 12 goes 1 time, remainder 2. Bring down 5: 10 into 25 goes 2 times, remainder 5. Quotient 612, remainder 5. Check: 612 x 10 + 5 = 6,125.

mcqs.q: What is 2,060 / 23?
mcqs.why: 23 into 206 goes 8 times (8 x 23 = 184), remainder 22. Bring down 0: 23 into 220 goes 9 times (9 x 23 = 207), remainder 13. Quotient 89, remainder 13. Check: 89 x 23 + 13 = 2,060.

mcqs.q: The steps of long division, in order, are:
options: Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, repeat
mcqs.why: Long division works from the left of the dividend: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down the next digit, and repeat until no digit is left.

mcqs.q: What is 1,848 / 88?
mcqs.why: 88 into 184 goes 2 times (2 x 88 = 176), remainder 8. Bring down 8: 88 into 88 goes 1 time, remainder 0. Quotient 21, remainder 0. Check: 21 x 88 = 1,848.

mcqs.q: What is 7,392 / 32?
mcqs.why: 32 into 73 goes 2 times, remainder 9. Bring down 9: 32 into 99 goes 3 times, remainder 3. Bring down 2: 32 into 32 goes 1 time, remainder 0. Quotient 231. Check: 231 x 32 = 7,392.

lessons.title: Division Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Read the question carefully. Write what is given and what you have to find. When a total is shared equally — the same number in every camp, row, box or cupboard — we divide. Use long division: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, repeat. Some questions in this exercise also use addition, subtraction or multiplication; read each part carefully. At the end, write the answer as a full sentence with its unit.

Worked example: Blankets in each relief camp (Exercise 2, Q2)

Given: In 45 relief camps, 2,205 blankets were distributed equally. To find: how many blankets each camp got. Operation: division — divide: 2,205 divided by 45.

Step 1: 45 into 220 goes 4 times (4 x 45 = 180), remainder 40.
Step 2: Bring down 5: 45 into 405 goes 9 times (9 x 45 = 405), remainder 0.
Answer: Each camp got 49 blankets.

Worked example: Chairs in one row (Exercise 2, Q3)

Given: 1,107 chairs are placed in 27 rows, with the same number of chairs in each row. To find: how many chairs there are in a row. Operation: division — divide: 1,107 divided by 27.

Step 1: 27 into 110 goes 4 times (4 x 27 = 108), remainder 2.
Step 2: Bring down 7: 27 into 27 goes 1 time (1 x 27 = 27), remainder 0.
Answer: There are 41 chairs in a row.

Worked example: Biscuits in one box (Exercise 2, Q4)

Given: 3,036 biscuits are packed equally in 11 boxes. To find: how many biscuits there are in a box. Operation: division — divide: 3,036 divided by 11.

Step 1: 11 into 30 goes 2 times (2 x 11 = 22), remainder 8.
Step 2: Bring down 3: 11 into 83 goes 7 times (7 x 11 = 77), remainder 6.
Step 3: Bring down 6: 11 into 66 goes 6 times (6 x 11 = 66), remainder 0.
Answer: There are 276 biscuits in a box.

Worked example: Books in each cupboard (Exercise 2, Q5)

Given: 6,666 books are to be kept equally in 33 cupboards in a library. To find: how many books there will be in each cupboard. Operation: division — divide: 6,666 divided by 33.

Step 1: 33 into 66 goes 2 times (2 x 33 = 66), remainder 0.
Step 2: Bring down 6: 33 into 6 goes 0 times, so write 0 in the quotient, remainder 6.
Step 3: Bring down 6: 33 into 66 goes 2 times (2 x 33 = 66), remainder 0.
Answer: There will be 202 books in each cupboard.

Worked example: Money Saad spent altogether (Exercise 2, Q6a)

Given: Saad bought 10 washing machines for Rs 78,950 and an oven for Rs 21,550. To find: how much money he spent altogether. Operation: addition — add: 78,950 + 21,550.

Step 1: Ones place: 0 + 0 = 0. Write 0.
Step 2: Tens place: 5 + 5 = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 9 + 5 + 1 (carry) = 15. Write 5 and carry 1.
Step 4: Thousands place: 8 + 1 + 1 (carry) = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 7 + 2 + 1 (carry) = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.
Step 6: Ten-thousands carry: write 1.
Answer: Saad spent Rs 100,500 altogether.

Worked example: How much more on washing machines than on the oven? (Exercise 2, Q6b)

Given: Washing machines cost Rs 78,950 and the oven cost Rs 21,550. To find: how much more amount he spent on washing machines than on an oven. Operation: subtraction — subtract: 78,950 - 21,550.

Step 1: Ones place: 0 - 0 = 0. Write 0.
Step 2: Tens place: 5 - 5 = 0. Write 0.
Step 3: Hundreds place: 9 - 5 = 4. Write 4.
Step 4: Thousands place: 8 - 1 = 7. Write 7.
Step 5: Ten-thousands place: 7 - 2 = 5. Write 5.
Answer: He spent Rs 57,400 more on washing machines than on the oven.

Worked example: Price of one washing machine (Exercise 2, Q6c)

Given: 10 washing machines cost Rs 78,950 in total. To find: how much amount he spent on one washing machine. Operation: division — divide: 78,950 divided by 10.

Step 1: 10 into 78 goes 7 times (7 x 10 = 70), remainder 8.
Step 2: Bring down 9: 10 into 89 goes 8 times (8 x 10 = 80), remainder 9.
Step 3: Bring down 5: 10 into 95 goes 9 times (9 x 10 = 90), remainder 5.
Step 4: Bring down 0: 10 into 50 goes 5 times (5 x 10 = 50), remainder 0.
Answer: He spent Rs 7,895 on one washing machine.

Worked example: Rice in one bag (Exercise 2, Q7a)

Given: In 30 bags, 1,350 kg rice are packed equally. To find: how many kilograms of rice are in one bag. Operation: division — divide: 1,350 divided by 30.

Step 1: 30 into 135 goes 4 times (4 x 30 = 120), remainder 15.
Step 2: Bring down 0: 30 into 150 goes 5 times (5 x 30 = 150), remainder 0.
Answer: There are 45 kg of rice in one bag.

Worked example: Rice in 38 bags (Exercise 2, Q7b)

Given: One bag holds 45 kg of rice (from Q7a). To find: how many kilograms of rice will be packed in 38 bags. Operation: multiplication — multiply: 45 x 38.

Step 1: Multiply 45 by 8 (8 ones): 45 x 8 = 360.
Step 2: Multiply 45 by 30 (3 tens): 45 x 30 = 1,350.
Step 3: Add the partial products: 360 + 1,350 = 1,710.
Answer: 1,710 kg of rice will be packed in 38 bags.

mcqs.q: In 45 relief camps, 2,205 blankets were distributed equally. How many blankets did each camp get?
mcqs.why: Sharing equally means divide: 2,205 / 45. 45 into 220 goes 4 times (4 x 45 = 180), remainder 40. Bring down 5: 45 into 405 goes 9 times, remainder 0. Each camp got 49 blankets.

mcqs.q: 1,107 chairs are placed in 27 rows with the same number in each row. How many chairs are in a row?
mcqs.why: Divide: 1,107 / 27. 27 into 110 goes 4 times (4 x 27 = 108), remainder 2. Bring down 7: 27 into 27 goes 1 time, remainder 0. There are 41 chairs in a row. Check: 41 x 27 = 1,107.

mcqs.q: 3,036 biscuits are packed equally in 11 boxes. How many biscuits are in a box?
mcqs.why: Divide: 3,036 / 11. 11 into 30 goes 2 times, remainder 8. Bring down 3: 11 into 83 goes 7 times, remainder 6. Bring down 6: 11 into 66 goes 6 times, remainder 0. There are 276 biscuits in a box.

mcqs.q: 6,666 books are to be kept equally in 33 cupboards. How many books will be in each cupboard?
mcqs.why: Divide: 6,666 / 33. 33 into 66 goes 2 times, remainder 0. Bring down 6: 33 into 6 goes 0 times, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 6: 33 into 66 goes 2 times, remainder 0. There will be 202 books in each cupboard.

mcqs.q: Saad bought 10 washing machines for Rs 78,950 and an oven for Rs 21,550. How much money did he spend altogether?
mcqs.why: Altogether means add: 78,950 + 21,550 = 100,500. Ones: 0 + 0 = 0. Tens: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Hundreds: 9 + 5 + 1 = 15, write 5 and carry 1. Thousands: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10. So Saad spent Rs 100,500.

mcqs.q: How much more did Saad spend on washing machines (Rs 78,950) than on the oven (Rs 21,550)?
mcqs.why: How much more means subtract: 78,950 - 21,550 = 57,400. Hundreds: 9 - 5 = 4; thousands: 8 - 1 = 7; ten-thousands: 7 - 2 = 5. He spent Rs 57,400 more.

mcqs.q: 10 washing machines cost Rs 78,950 in total. How much did Saad spend on one washing machine?
mcqs.why: Divide the total by 10: 78,950 / 10 = 7,895. He spent Rs 7,895 on one washing machine.

mcqs.q: In 30 bags, 1,350 kg rice is packed equally. How many kilograms of rice are in one bag?
mcqs.why: Divide: 1,350 / 30. 30 into 135 goes 4 times (4 x 30 = 120), remainder 15. Bring down 0: 30 into 150 goes 5 times, remainder 0. There are 45 kg of rice in one bag.

mcqs.q: One bag holds 45 kg of rice. How many kilograms of rice will be packed in 38 bags?
mcqs.why: Multiply: 45 x 38. 45 x 8 = 360 and 45 x 30 = 1,350. Add the partial products: 360 + 1,350 = 1,710 kg.

mcqs.q: When a total is shared equally, with the same number in every camp, row, box or cupboard, we:
mcqs.why: Equal sharing is division: use long division (divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, repeat) and write the answer as a full sentence with its unit.

lessons.title: Number Patterns
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

A pattern is a list of numbers that follows a rule. To find the rule, look at how each number changes to make the next number: is the same number added each time, or is the same number subtracted each time? Once you know the rule, use it again and again to find the next terms.

Worked example: 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, __, __ (Exercise 3, Q1a)

Step 1: Find the rule: 15 - 11 = 4, 19 - 15 = 4, 23 - 19 = 4. The rule is: adding 4 each time.
Step 2: Next term: 27 + 4 = 31.
Step 3: Next term: 31 + 4 = 35.
Answer: 31, 35

Worked example: 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, __, __ (Exercise 3, Q1b)

Step 1: Find the rule: 60 - 30 = 30, 90 - 60 = 30, 120 - 90 = 30. The rule is: adding 30 each time.
Step 2: Next term: 150 + 30 = 180.
Step 3: Next term: 180 + 30 = 210.
Answer: 180, 210

Worked example: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, __, __ (Exercise 3, Q1c)

Step 1: Find the rule: 12 - 6 = 6, 18 - 12 = 6, 24 - 18 = 6. The rule is: adding 6 each time.
Step 2: Next term: 30 + 6 = 36.
Step 3: Next term: 36 + 6 = 42.
Answer: 36, 42

Step 1: Find the rule: 850 - 800 = 50, 800 - 750 = 50, 750 - 700 = 50. The rule is: subtracting 50 each time.

Step 3: Next term: 600 - 50 = 550.

Step 3: Next term: 91 - 3 = 88.

Worked example: Patterns in the hundreds chart (Exercise 3, Q2)

Step 1: Pattern 1 — Moving right across a row adds 1 each time (for example 1, 2, 3, 4).
Step 2: Pattern 2 — Moving down a column adds 10 each time (for example 1, 11, 21, 31).
Step 3: Pattern 3 — Moving left across a row subtracts 1 each time.
Step 4: Pattern 4 — Moving up a column subtracts 10 each time.
Step 5: Pattern 5 — Moving diagonally down-right adds 11 each time (for example 1, 12, 23, 34).
Step 6: Other correct patterns in the chart: even numbers go 2, 4, 6, 8 (adding 2 each time), and multiples of 10 go 10, 20, 30 (adding 10 each time).

lessons.title: Exercise 1: Divisibility by 2, 3, 5 and 10 (book page 38)
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6 or 8). A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. A number is divisible by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5. A number is divisible by 10 if it ends in 0.

Worked example: Divisible by 2 (Exercise 1, Q1)

Step 1: Look at the last digit of each number.
Step 1: 16 ends in 6, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Step 2: 43 ends in 3, which is odd, so it is NOT divisible by 2
Step 3: 98 ends in 8, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Step 4: 134 ends in 4, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Step 5: 6,781 ends in 1, which is odd, so it is NOT divisible by 2
Step 6: 2,114 ends in 4, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Step 7: 9,226 ends in 6, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Step 8: 67 ends in 7, which is odd, so it is NOT divisible by 2
Step 9: 540 ends in 0, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Step 10: 82,420 ends in 0, which is even, so it is divisible by 2
Answer: Divisible by 2: 16, 98, 134, 2,114, 9,226, 540, 82,420. Not divisible by 2: 43, 6,781, 67

Worked example: Divisible by 3 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: 20: digit sum = 2+0 = 2, and 2 is NOT divisible by 3, so 20 is NOT divisible by 3
Step 2: 27: digit sum = 2+7 = 9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so 27 is divisible by 3
Step 3: 165: digit sum = 1+6+5 = 12, and 12 is divisible by 3, so 165 is divisible by 3
Step 4: 125: digit sum = 1+2+5 = 8, and 8 is NOT divisible by 3, so 125 is NOT divisible by 3
Step 5: 6,720: digit sum = 6+7+2+0 = 15, and 15 is divisible by 3, so 6,720 is divisible by 3
Step 6: 8,955: digit sum = 8+9+5+5 = 27, and 27 is divisible by 3, so 8,955 is divisible by 3
Step 7: 52,110: digit sum = 5+2+1+1+0 = 9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so 52,110 is divisible by 3
Step 8: 21,945: digit sum = 2+1+9+4+5 = 21, and 21 is divisible by 3, so 21,945 is divisible by 3
Answer: Divisible by 3: 27, 165, 6,720, 8,955, 52,110, 21,945. Not divisible by 3: 20, 125

Worked example: Divisible by 5 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: 30 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 5
Step 2: 50 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 5
Step 3: 7,895 ends in 5, so it is divisible by 5
Step 4: 2,298 ends in 8, so it is NOT divisible by 5
Answer: Divisible by 5: 30, 50, 7,895. Not divisible by 5: 2,298

Worked example: Divisible by 10 (Exercise 1, Q4)

Step 1: 56,560 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 10
Step 2: 1,982 ends in 2, so it is NOT divisible by 10
Step 3: 42,420 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 10
Step 4: 130 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 10
Answer: Divisible by 10: 56,560, 42,420, 130. Not divisible by 10: 1,982

mcqs.q: A number is divisible by 2 if:
options: Its last digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6 or 8)
mcqs.why: The rule for 2 is about the last digit only: if the last digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6 or 8), the number is divisible by 2.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
mcqs.why: 9,226 ends in 6, which is even, so it is divisible by 2. The numbers 43, 6,781 and 67 end in 3, 1 and 7, which are odd, so they are not divisible by 2.

mcqs.q: A number is divisible by 3 if:
options: The sum of its digits is divisible by 3
mcqs.why: For 3 we add all the digits: if the digit sum is divisible by 3, the number itself is divisible by 3.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 3?
mcqs.why: Digit sum of 8,955: 8 + 9 + 5 + 5 = 27, and 27 is divisible by 3, so 8,955 is divisible by 3. The digit sum of 20 is 2 and of 125 is 8, neither divisible by 3.

mcqs.q: Which number is NOT divisible by 5?
mcqs.why: A number is divisible by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5. 2,298 ends in 8, so it is not divisible by 5. 30 and 50 end in 0, and 7,895 ends in 5.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 10?
mcqs.why: A number is divisible by 10 if it ends in 0. 56,560 ends in 0. 1,982 ends in 2, and 42,425 and 1,305 end in 5.

mcqs.q: The digit sum of 52,110 is:
mcqs.why: Add the digits: 5 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 9. Since 9 is divisible by 3, the number 52,110 is divisible by 3.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by both 2 and 5?
mcqs.why: 82,420 ends in 0: the even last digit 0 makes it divisible by 2, and ending in 0 also makes it divisible by 5.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 3?
mcqs.why: Digit sum of 21,945: 2 + 1 + 9 + 4 + 5 = 21, and 21 is divisible by 3, so 21,945 is divisible by 3.

mcqs.q: 6,720 is divisible by 3 because:
options: Its digit sum 6 + 7 + 2 + 0 = 15 is divisible by 3
mcqs.why: For divisibility by 3, add the digits: 6 + 7 + 2 + 0 = 15, and 15 is divisible by 3, so 6,720 is divisible by 3.

lessons.title: Exercise 2: Prime and Composite Numbers, Factors and Multiples (book pages 41-42)
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A composite number has more than two factors. A factor of a number divides it exactly with no remainder. A multiple of a number is the number multiplied by 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on.

Worked example: Composite numbers between 30 and 50 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: Check every number from 31 to 49. A number is composite if it has a factor other than 1 and itself.
Step 2: 32 = 2 x 16, 33 = 3 x 11, 34 = 2 x 17, 35 = 5 x 7, 36 = 6 x 6, 38 = 2 x 19, 39 = 3 x 13, 40 = 4 x 10, 42 = 6 x 7, 44 = 4 x 11, 45 = 5 x 9, 46 = 2 x 23, 48 = 6 x 8, 49 = 7 x 7.
Step 3: The remaining numbers 31, 37, 41, 43 and 47 are prime, so they are not composite.
Answer: 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 38, 39, 40, 42, 44, 45, 46, 48, 49

Worked example: Encircle the prime numbers (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: Test each number for factors other than 1 and itself.
Step 2: 15 = 3 x 5 (composite), 31 has only factors 1 and 31 (prime), 42 = 6 x 7 (composite), 67 has only factors 1 and 67 (prime).
Step 3: 11 has only factors 1 and 11 (prime), 52 = 4 x 13 (composite), 98 = 2 x 49 (composite), 89 has only factors 1 and 89 (prime).
Answer: Prime numbers: 31, 67, 11, 89

Step 2: Count them until you have 15 prime numbers.

mcqs.why: Find pairs that multiply to make 15: 1 x 15 = 15 and 3 x 5 = 15. Writing all the different numbers from these pairs, the factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15.

mcqs.why: Pairs that multiply to make 49: 1 x 49 = 49 and 7 x 7 = 49. Writing each different number once, the factors of 49 are 1, 7, 49.

lessons.title: Exercise 3: Prime Factorisation, Common Prime Factors and First Common Multiples (book pages 45-46)
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Prime factorisation means writing a number as a product of prime numbers only, by dividing it again and again by the smallest prime factor. A common prime factor is a prime factor that appears in the factorisation of every given number. The first common multiple is the smallest multiple shared by all the given numbers (also called the LCM).

Worked example: Prime factors of 17 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: 17 cannot be divided by any smaller prime number.
Step 2: So 17 is itself a prime number.
Answer: 17 = 17

Worked example: Prime factors of 21 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: 21 / 3 = 7
Step 2: 7 is prime, so we stop
Step 3: Collect the divisors used: 3 x 7.
Step 4: Check: 3 x 7 = 21.
Answer: 21 = 3 x 7

Worked example: Prime factors of 18 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: 18 / 2 = 9
Step 2: 9 / 3 = 3
Step 3: 3 / 3 = 1
Step 4: Collect the divisors used: 2 x 3 x 3.
Step 5: Check: 2 x 3 x 3 = 18.
Answer: 18 = 2 x 3 x 3

Worked example: Prime factors of 34 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: 34 / 2 = 17
Step 2: 17 is prime, so we stop
Step 3: Collect the divisors used: 2 x 17.
Step 4: Check: 2 x 17 = 34.
Answer: 34 = 2 x 17

Worked example: Prime factors of 44 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: 44 / 2 = 22
Step 2: 22 / 2 = 11
Step 3: 11 is prime, so we stop
Step 4: Collect the divisors used: 2 x 2 x 11.
Step 5: Check: 2 x 2 x 11 = 44.
Answer: 44 = 2 x 2 x 11

Worked example: Prime factors of 33 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: 33 / 3 = 11
Step 2: 11 is prime, so we stop

Step 4: Check: 3 x 11 = 33.

Step 2: Compare the factorisations and look for primes that appear in every one.

Answer: Common prime factors: none — no prime factor is common to all of them

Worked example: Common prime factors of 4, 8 (Exercise 3, Q2)

Step 1: Write the prime factorisation of each number: 4 = 2 x 2; 8 = 2 x 2 x 2.
Step 2: Compare the factorisations and look for primes that appear in every one.
Step 3: The prime factors common to all of them are: 2, 2.
Answer: Common prime factors: 2, 2

mcqs.q: The prime factorisation of 18 is:
mcqs.why: Divide by the smallest prime factor again and again: 18 / 2 = 9, 9 / 3 = 3 and 3 / 3 = 1. Collect the divisors used: 2 x 3 x 3. Check: 2 x 3 x 3 = 18.

mcqs.q: The prime factorisation of 44 is:
mcqs.why: 44 / 2 = 22 and 22 / 2 = 11, and 11 is prime so we stop. Collect the divisors used: 2 x 2 x 11. Check: 2 x 2 x 11 = 44.

mcqs.q: The prime factorisation of 48 is:
mcqs.why: 48 / 2 = 24, 24 / 2 = 12, 12 / 2 = 6 and 6 / 2 = 3, and 3 is prime. Collect the divisors used: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3. Check: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 48.

mcqs.q: The prime factorisation of 17 is:
mcqs.why: 17 cannot be divided by any smaller prime number, so 17 is itself a prime number and its prime factorisation is just 17.

mcqs.q: The common prime factors of 10 and 20 are:
mcqs.why: Write the factorisations: 10 = 2 x 5 and 20 = 2 x 2 x 5. The prime factors that appear in every factorisation are 2 and 5.

mcqs.q: The common prime factor of 7, 21 and 28 is:
mcqs.why: 7 = 7, 21 = 3 x 7 and 28 = 2 x 2 x 7. The only prime factor that appears in every factorisation is 7.

mcqs.q: The numbers 5, 30 and 12 have:
mcqs.why: 5 = 5, 30 = 2 x 3 x 5 and 12 = 2 x 2 x 3. No prime appears in every factorisation: 5 is missing from 12, and 2 and 3 are missing from 5, so there is no common prime factor.

mcqs.q: The first common multiple of 9 and 12 is:
mcqs.why: List multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36. 36 is also a multiple of 9 because 36 / 9 = 4, and no smaller multiple of 12 is a multiple of 9, so the first common multiple is 36.

mcqs.q: The first common multiple of 10, 20 and 30 is:
mcqs.why: 60 is a multiple of all of them: 60 / 10 = 6, 60 / 20 = 3 and 60 / 30 = 2. No smaller number is a multiple of all three, so it is the first common multiple.

mcqs.q: The first common multiple of 6 and 15 is:
mcqs.why: List multiples of 15: 15, 30. 30 is also a multiple of 6 because 30 / 6 = 5, so the first common multiple of 6 and 15 is 30.

lessons.title: Exercise 1: Like and Unlike Fractions, Comparing, Lowest Form and Mixed Numbers (book pages 58-59)
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

Like fractions have the same denominator; unlike fractions have different denominators. To compare fractions, make the denominators the same, then compare the numerators. The lowest form of a fraction is made by dividing the numerator and denominator by their HCF until no common factor remains except 1. A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. A mixed number has a whole part and a proper fraction part. To change an improper fraction into a mixed number, divide the numerator by the denominator: the quotient is the whole part and the remainder is the new numerator. To change a mixed number into an improper fraction, multiply the whole part by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.

Worked example: Unlike fractions (Exercise 1, Q1)

Step 1: (a) 3/5 and 1/2 have denominators 5 and 2 — different, so they are unlike.
Step 2: (b) 7/9 and 4/9 both have denominator 9 — like. (c) 6/11 and 1/11 both have denominator 11 — like. (d) 2/8 and 3/8 both have denominator 8 — like.
Step 3: (e) 6/10 and 1/5 have denominators 10 and 5 — different, so they are unlike. (f) 5/9 and 2/7 have denominators 9 and 7 — different, so they are unlike.
Answer: Unlike pairs: (a) 3/5 and 1/2, (e) 6/10 and 1/5, (f) 5/9 and 2/7

Worked example: Compare 1/2 and 1/2 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 2 and 2 is 2.
Step 2: 1/2 = 1/2 and 1/2 = 1/2.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 1 = 1.
Answer: 1/2 = 1/2

Worked example: Compare 4/5 and 9/10 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 5 and 10 is 10.
Step 2: 4/5 = 8/10 and 9/10 = 9/10.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 8 < 9.
Answer: 4/5 < 9/10

Worked example: Compare 1/2 and 1/2 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 2 and 2 is 2.
Step 2: 1/2 = 1/2 and 1/2 = 1/2.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 1 = 1.
Answer: 1/2 = 1/2

Worked example: Compare 1/7 and 5/8 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 7 and 8 is 56.
Step 2: 1/7 = 8/56 and 5/8 = 35/56.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 8 < 35.
Answer: 1/7 < 5/8

Worked example: Compare 2/9 and 5/6 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 9 and 6 is 18.
Step 2: 2/9 = 4/18 and 5/6 = 15/18.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 4 < 15.
Answer: 2/9 < 5/6

Worked example: Compare 2/3 and 5/7 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 3 and 7 is 21.
Step 2: 2/3 = 14/21 and 5/7 = 15/21.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 14 < 15.
Answer: 2/3 < 5/7

Worked example: Compare 1/3 and 1/4 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 3 and 4 is 12.
Step 2: 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 4 > 3.
Answer: 1/3 > 1/4

Worked example: Compare 4/11 and 7/10 (Exercise 1, Q2)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 11 and 10 is 110.
Step 2: 4/11 = 40/110 and 7/10 = 77/110.
Step 3: Compare the numerators: 40 < 77.
Answer: 4/11 < 7/10

Worked example: Lowest form of 4/20 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 4 and 20 is 4.
Step 2: Divide both by 4: 4 / 4 = 1 and 20 / 4 = 5.
Answer: 4/20 = 1/5

Worked example: Lowest form of 2/12 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 2 and 12 is 2.
Step 2: Divide both by 2: 2 / 2 = 1 and 12 / 2 = 6.
Answer: 2/12 = 1/6

Worked example: Lowest form of 30/45 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 30 and 45 is 15.
Step 2: Divide both by 15: 30 / 15 = 2 and 45 / 15 = 3.
Answer: 30/45 = 2/3

Worked example: Lowest form of 9/27 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 9 and 27 is 9.
Step 2: Divide both by 9: 9 / 9 = 1 and 27 / 9 = 3.
Answer: 9/27 = 1/3

Worked example: Lowest form of 12/16 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 12 and 16 is 4.
Step 2: Divide both by 4: 12 / 4 = 3 and 16 / 4 = 4.
Answer: 12/16 = 3/4

Worked example: Lowest form of 15/25 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 15 and 25 is 5.
Step 2: Divide both by 5: 15 / 5 = 3 and 25 / 5 = 5.
Answer: 15/25 = 3/5

Worked example: Lowest form of 16/24 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 16 and 24 is 8.
Step 2: Divide both by 8: 16 / 8 = 2 and 24 / 8 = 3.
Answer: 16/24 = 2/3

Worked example: Lowest form of 4/18 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 4 and 18 is 2.
Step 2: Divide both by 2: 4 / 2 = 2 and 18 / 2 = 9.
Answer: 4/18 = 2/9

Worked example: Lowest form of 14/20 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 14 and 20 is 2.
Step 2: Divide both by 2: 14 / 2 = 7 and 20 / 2 = 10.
Answer: 14/20 = 7/10

Worked example: Lowest form of 17/34 (Exercise 1, Q3)

Step 1: The HCF of 17 and 34 is 17.
Step 2: Divide both by 17: 17 / 17 = 1 and 34 / 17 = 2.
Answer: 17/34 = 1/2

Worked example: Proper fractions and mixed numbers (Exercise 1, Q4)

Step 1: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator: 2/5, 7/8, 3/4, 3/8, 9/11 and 6/7 all have a smaller numerator.
Step 2: A mixed number has a whole part with a fraction part: 3 4/7, 1 1/2, 3 7/11 and 11 1/2.
Answer: Proper fractions: 2/5, 7/8, 3/4, 3/8, 9/11, 6/7. Mixed numbers: 3 4/7, 1 1/2, 3 7/11, 11 1/2

Worked example: Change 8/5 into a mixed number (Exercise 1, Q5)

Step 1: Divide 8 by 5: 8 / 5 = 1 remainder 3.
Step 2: The quotient 1 is the whole part and the remainder 3 becomes the numerator over 5.
Answer: 8/5 = 1 3/5

Worked example: Change 11/5 into a mixed number (Exercise 1, Q5)

Step 1: Divide 11 by 5: 11 / 5 = 2 remainder 1.
Step 2: The quotient 2 is the whole part and the remainder 1 becomes the numerator over 5.
Answer: 11/5 = 2 1/5

Worked example: Change 13/10 into a mixed number (Exercise 1, Q5)

Step 1: Divide 13 by 10: 13 / 10 = 1 remainder 3.
Step 2: The quotient 1 is the whole part and the remainder 3 becomes the numerator over 10.
Answer: 13/10 = 1 3/10

Worked example: Change 20/9 into a mixed number (Exercise 1, Q5)

Step 1: Divide 20 by 9: 20 / 9 = 2 remainder 2.
Step 2: The quotient 2 is the whole part and the remainder 2 becomes the numerator over 9.
Answer: 20/9 = 2 2/9

Worked example: Change 15/2 into a mixed number (Exercise 1, Q5)

Step 1: Divide 15 by 2: 15 / 2 = 7 remainder 1.
Step 2: The quotient 7 is the whole part and the remainder 1 becomes the numerator over 2.
Answer: 15/2 = 7 1/2

Worked example: Change 2 3/5 into an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q6)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 2 x 5 = 10.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 10 + 3 = 13.
Step 3: Write 13 over the same denominator 5.
Answer: 2 3/5 = 13/5

Worked example: Change 7 5/6 into an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q6)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 7 x 6 = 42.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 42 + 5 = 47.
Step 3: Write 47 over the same denominator 6.
Answer: 7 5/6 = 47/6

Worked example: Change 4 1/7 into an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q6)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 4 x 7 = 28.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 28 + 1 = 29.
Step 3: Write 29 over the same denominator 7.
Answer: 4 1/7 = 29/7

Worked example: Change 5 3/11 into an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q6)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 5 x 11 = 55.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 55 + 3 = 58.
Step 3: Write 58 over the same denominator 11.
Answer: 5 3/11 = 58/11

Worked example: Change 6 1/3 into an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q6)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 6 x 3 = 18.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 18 + 1 = 19.
Step 3: Write 19 over the same denominator 3.
Answer: 6 1/3 = 19/3

Worked example: Change 2 4/13 into an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q6)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 2 x 13 = 26.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 26 + 4 = 30.
Step 3: Write 30 over the same denominator 13.
Answer: 2 4/13 = 30/13

Worked example: Order 3/5, 3/9, 3/7 (Exercise 1, Q7a)

Step 1: All three fractions have the same numerator 3.
Step 2: With the same numerator, the larger the denominator, the smaller the fraction.
Step 3: Denominators in order: 9 is largest, then 7, then 5.
Answer: Ascending: 3/9, 3/7, 3/5. Descending: 3/5, 3/7, 3/9

Worked example: Order 3/4, 1/3, 6/7 (Exercise 1, Q7b)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 4, 3, 7 is 84.
Step 2: 3/4 = 63/84, 1/3 = 28/84, 6/7 = 72/84.
Step 3: Now order the fractions by their new numerators.
Answer: Ascending: 1/3, 3/4, 6/7. Descending: 6/7, 3/4, 1/3

Worked example: Order 3/5, 1/5, 4/15 (Exercise 1, Q7c)

Step 1: Make the denominators the same. LCM of 5, 5, 15 is 15.
Step 2: 3/5 = 9/15, 1/5 = 3/15, 4/15 = 4/15.
Step 3: Now order the fractions by their new numerators.
Answer: Ascending: 1/5, 4/15, 3/5. Descending: 3/5, 4/15, 1/5

Worked example: Three full and one half pizza (Exercise 1, Q8)

Step 1: The three full pizzas give the whole part 3.
Step 2: The half pizza gives the fraction part 1/2.
Step 3: Join the whole part and the fraction part.
Answer: 3 1/2

Worked example: 1 1/2 kg as an improper fraction (Exercise 1, Q9)

Step 1: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 1 x 2 = 2.
Step 2: Add the numerator: 2 + 1 = 3.
Step 3: Write 3 over the same denominator 2.
Answer: 1 1/2 = 3/2 kg

Worked example: Try It! Who am I? (book page 58)

Step 1: The number is between 2 and 10 and nearer to 8 than to 4, so its whole part is 7 or 8.
Step 2: The whole part must be odd, and 7 is odd while 8 is even, so the whole part is 7.
Step 3: Take the fraction part as 1/2, which keeps the number nearer to 8 than to 4.
Step 4: Check: 7 1/2 is between 2 and 10, it is nearer to 8 than to 4, and its whole part 7 is odd.
Answer: 7 1/2

mcqs.q: Like fractions are fractions that have:
options: A numerator bigger than the denominator
mcqs.why: Like fractions have the same denominator, like 7/9 and 4/9. Unlike fractions have different denominators, like 3/5 and 1/2.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows unlike fractions?
mcqs.why: 3/5 and 1/2 have denominators 5 and 2, which are different, so they are unlike. The other pairs share the same denominator, so they are like fractions.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is greater: 4/5 or 9/10?
mcqs.why: Make the denominators the same: the LCM of 5 and 10 is 10, and 4/5 = 8/10. Compare the numerators: 8 is less than 9, so 4/5 < 9/10 and 9/10 is greater.

mcqs.q: The lowest form of 30/45 is:
mcqs.why: The HCF of 30 and 45 is 15. Divide both by 15: 30 / 15 = 2 and 45 / 15 = 3, so 30/45 = 2/3.

mcqs.q: The lowest form of 12/16 is:
mcqs.why: The HCF of 12 and 16 is 4. Divide both by 4: 12 / 4 = 3 and 16 / 4 = 4, so 12/16 = 3/4.

mcqs.q: 8/5 as a mixed number is:
mcqs.why: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 8 / 5 gives quotient 1 and remainder 3. The quotient is the whole part and the remainder is the new numerator over 5, so 8/5 = 1 3/5.

mcqs.q: 2 3/5 as an improper fraction is:
mcqs.why: Multiply the whole part by the denominator and add the numerator: 2 x 5 = 10 and 10 + 3 = 13. Write 13 over the same denominator 5, so 2 3/5 = 13/5.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is a proper fraction?
mcqs.why: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator: in 3/4, 3 is less than 4. In 8/5, 5/3 and 7/4 the numerator is bigger than the denominator.

mcqs.q: The fractions 3/5, 3/9 and 3/7 have the same numerator. The smallest of them is:
mcqs.why: With the same numerator, the larger the denominator, the smaller the fraction. 9 is the largest denominator, so 3/9 is the smallest; ascending order is 3/9, 3/7, 3/5.

mcqs.q: Three full pizzas and one half pizza make the mixed number:
mcqs.why: The three full pizzas give the whole part 3 and the half pizza gives the fraction part 1/2. Joining the whole part and the fraction part gives 3 1/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 2: Adding and Subtracting Like Fractions (book page 62)
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

To add or subtract like fractions, keep the same denominator and add or subtract only the numerators. Then write the answer in its lowest form, and change an improper fraction answer into a mixed number. To find the difference between two like fractions, subtract the smallest fraction from the greatest fraction.

Worked example: Add 6/7 + 5/7 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: The denominators are the same (7), so add the numerators: 6 + 5 = 11.
Step 2: 6/7 + 5/7 = 11/7.
Step 3: Change the improper fraction into a mixed number: 11 / 7 = 1 remainder 4, giving 1 4/7.
Answer: 6/7 + 5/7 = 11/7 = 1 4/7

Worked example: Add 11/13 + 11/13 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: The denominators are the same (13), so add the numerators: 11 + 11 = 22.
Step 2: 11/13 + 11/13 = 22/13.
Step 3: Change the improper fraction into a mixed number: 22 / 13 = 1 remainder 9, giving 1 9/13.
Answer: 11/13 + 11/13 = 22/13 = 1 9/13

Worked example: Add 5/17 + 11/17 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: The denominators are the same (17), so add the numerators: 5 + 11 = 16.
Step 2: 5/17 + 11/17 = 16/17.
Answer: 5/17 + 11/17 = 16/17

Worked example: Add 7/15 + 8/15 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: The denominators are the same (15), so add the numerators: 7 + 8 = 1.
Step 2: 7/15 + 8/15 = 1/1.
Step 3: 15/15 means one whole, which is 1.
Answer: 7/15 + 8/15 = 1

Worked example: Add 5/16 + 5/16 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: The denominators are the same (16), so add the numerators: 5 + 5 = 5.
Step 2: 5/16 + 5/16 = 5/8.
Answer: 5/16 + 5/16 = 5/8

Worked example: Add 2/19 + 12/19 (Exercise 2, Q1)

Step 1: The denominators are the same (19), so add the numerators: 2 + 12 = 14.
Step 2: 2/19 + 12/19 = 14/19.
Answer: 2/19 + 12/19 = 14/19

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 2/3, 1/1 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 1/1 and the smallest fraction is 2/3.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 1 - 2 = -1.
Step 3: 1/1 - 2/3 = -1/1.
Step 4: Write in lowest form by dividing by 1: 1/3.
Answer: 1/1 - 2/3 = 1/3

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 1/11, 7/11 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 7/11 and the smallest fraction is 1/11.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 7 - 1 = 6.
Step 3: 7/11 - 1/11 = 6/11.
Answer: 7/11 - 1/11 = 6/11

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 11/12, 7/12 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 11/12 and the smallest fraction is 7/12.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 11 - 7 = 4.
Step 3: 11/12 - 7/12 = 4/12.
Answer: 11/12 - 7/12 = 1/3

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 1/3, 5/7 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 5/7 and the smallest fraction is 1/3.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 5 - 1 = 4.
Step 3: 5/7 - 1/3 = 4/7.
Step 4: Write in lowest form by dividing by 1: 8/21.
Answer: 5/7 - 1/3 = 8/21

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 2/5, 4/5 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 4/5 and the smallest fraction is 2/5.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 4 - 2 = 2.
Step 3: 4/5 - 2/5 = 2/5.
Answer: 4/5 - 2/5 = 2/5

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 4/5, 2/5 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 4/5 and the smallest fraction is 2/5.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 4 - 2 = 2.
Step 3: 4/5 - 2/5 = 2/5.
Answer: 4/5 - 2/5 = 2/5

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 2/13, 1/13 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 2/13 and the smallest fraction is 1/13.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 2 - 1 = 1.
Step 3: 2/13 - 1/13 = 1/13.
Answer: 2/13 - 1/13 = 1/13

Worked example: Greatest minus smallest: 1/3, 1/5 (Exercise 2, Q2)

Step 1: The greatest fraction is 1/3 and the smallest fraction is 1/5.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 1 - 1 = 0.
Step 3: 1/3 - 1/5 = 0/3.
Step 4: Write in lowest form by dividing by 1: 2/15.
Answer: 1/3 - 1/5 = 2/15

Worked example: Wall painted in two days (Exercise 2, Q3a)

Step 1: Add the two parts: 7/13 + 3/13.
Step 2: The denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 7 + 3 = 10.
Answer: 7/13 + 3/13 = 10/13 part of the wall

Worked example: Which day was more painted? (Exercise 2, Q3b)

Step 1: Compare 7/13 (first day) and 3/13 (second day): 7 is greater than 3, so more was painted on the first day.
Step 2: Subtract: 7/13 - 3/13, so 7 - 3 = 4 over 13.
Answer: First day, by 4/13 part more

Worked example: Total fertilizer used (Exercise 2, Q4)

Step 1: Add: 5/14 + 7/14.
Step 2: Add the numerators: 5 + 7 = 12, giving 12/14.
Step 3: Divide numerator and denominator by 2 for the lowest form: 12/14 = 6/7.
Answer: 5/14 + 7/14 = 6/7 kg

Worked example: Homework time of two sisters (Exercise 2, Q5)

Step 1: Add: 2/10 + 7/10.
Step 2: Add the numerators: 2 + 7 = 9, giving 9/10.
Answer: 2/10 + 7/10 = 9/10 hours

Worked example: Who has more profit share? (Exercise 2, Q6)

Step 1: Compare 7/11 (Shiraz) and 10/11 (Omar): 10 is greater than 7, so Omar has more.
Step 2: Subtract: 10/11 - 7/11, so 10 - 7 = 3 over 11.
Answer: Omar has more, by 3/11 share

mcqs.q: 6/7 + 5/7 is equal to:
mcqs.why: The denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 6 + 5 = 11, giving 11/7. Change the improper fraction into a mixed number: 11/7 = 1 4/7.

mcqs.q: 5/17 + 11/17 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Keep the same denominator and add only the numerators: 5 + 11 = 16, so 5/17 + 11/17 = 16/17.

mcqs.q: 7/15 + 8/15 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Add the numerators: 7 + 8 = 15, giving 15/15. 15/15 means one whole, which is 1.

mcqs.q: 5/16 + 5/16 in lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Add the numerators: 5 + 5 = 10, giving 10/16. Divide the numerator and denominator by 2 for the lowest form: 10/16 = 5/8.

mcqs.q: 7/11 - 1/11 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Subtract only the numerators and keep the same denominator: 7 - 1 = 6, so 7/11 - 1/11 = 6/11.

mcqs.q: 11/12 - 7/12 in lowest form is:
mcqs.why: Subtract the numerators: 11 - 7 = 4, giving 4/12. Divide the numerator and denominator by 4 for the lowest form: 4/12 = 1/3.

mcqs.q: A wall is painted in two days: 7/13 on the first day and 3/13 on the second day. The total part painted is:
mcqs.why: Add the two parts: 7/13 + 3/13. The denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 7 + 3 = 10. The total is 10/13 of the wall.

mcqs.q: For the same wall (7/13 on day one, 3/13 on day two), on which day was more painted, and by how much?
mcqs.why: Compare 7/13 and 3/13: 7 is greater than 3, so more was painted on the first day. The difference is 7/13 - 3/13 = 4/13.

mcqs.q: 5/14 + 7/14 in lowest form (the total fertilizer used, in kg) is:
mcqs.why: Add the numerators: 5 + 7 = 12, giving 12/14. Divide the numerator and denominator by 2 for the lowest form: 12/14 = 6/7 kg.

mcqs.q: Shiraz has 7/11 profit share and Omar has 10/11. Omar has more by:
mcqs.why: Compare 7/11 and 10/11: 10 is greater than 7, so Omar has more. Subtract the numerators: 10 - 7 = 3, so 10/11 - 7/11 = 3/11.

lessons.title: Exercise 3: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions (book page 66)
lessons.notes_html:
The rule

To multiply a fraction by a whole number, multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the same denominator, then simplify. To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators together and the denominators together, changing any mixed number into an improper fraction first, then simplify. To divide a fraction by a whole number, multiply the fraction by the reciprocal of the whole number (for example, dividing by 2 means multiplying by 1/2).

Worked example: Multiply: 6/7 x 4 (Exercise 3, Q1)

Step 1: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same.
Step 2: The product is 3 3/7 after simplifying.
Answer: 6/7 x 4 = 3 3/7
